chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi narrated, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far al-Nakha'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and others, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both)

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about the best of the servants, so he said: 'They are those who rejoice when they do good, and seek forgiveness when they do evil, and give thanks when they are given, and show patience when tested, and forgive when they are angry.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five characteristics of the best people according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith presents a comprehensive model of spiritual equilibrium, balancing joy in virtue with humility in repentance. It emphasizes that true excellence lies not in perfection, but in the immediate, balanced response to life's fluctuations—gratitude in prosperity and patience in adversity—reflecting the Shia emphasis on *muraqabah* (awareness of God) in daily conduct.
